title: Ceres Labs — Serving fit exploratory
summary: Initial discovery to understand Ceres Labs' current OpenAI + vLLM stack, pain points around latency and cost, and constraints for a private hosting option. Customer is interested in migration paths, eval parity for prompts, and security controls (KMS, audit logs, SSO). Agreed to run a small benchmark and share security docs; SE to propose pilot scope.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2 report (Jordan)
Samira to propose pilot test plan and benchmark script (Samira)
Ceres to share sample prompt set and 48h traffic profile (Miguel)
Schedule SE deep dive for private deployment networking (week of 11/16)
action_items: Jordan: Email security docs and compliance overview by 2026-11-12
Samira: Draft pilot scope + benchmark script by 2026-11-13
Miguel: Provide prompt set and token distribution by 2026-11-13
Owen: Provide list of required encryption/KMS controls by 2026-11-15
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): All right thanks everyone for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. We got Samira on the line as well, our SE, and Liam. How's everyone doing at Ceres?
[00:10] Priya (CTO): Hi thanks, doing well. We appreciate you carving time. We want to talk through whether Redwood can be a direct replacement for our current stack — we use OpenAI hosted for prod and vLLM at the edge for cheaper inference in batch.
[00:25] Samira (SE): Great, yeah, can you walk me through the current flow, roughly volumes, latencies that are important, and any constraints like data residency or KMS?
[00:32] Miguel (Lead ML): Sure. So prod is OpenAI ChatCompletion right now, about 200k tokens per day, peak qps maybe 6–8 requests per second, generation lengths about 300 tokens avg. For some internal batch jobs we run vLLM/TGI on prem for long-context scoring — that's a separate cluster. Biggest pain: cost at scale on OpenAI and occasional latency spikes; also we have to manage KV cache across vLLM instances which is gnarly.
[00:55] Jordan (AE): Got it. That's a pretty common pattern. Quick follow — are you exploring Redwood Hosted first or thinking about Dedicated / Private directly?
[01:04] Priya: We're considering both. Ideally we'd pilot on Hosted to prove parity then move to Dedicated or Private for data controls. We're in regulated research so KMS and audit logs are required, and we may need a VPC/private deployment later.
[01:18] Samira: Makes sense. From a compatibility perspective, you mentioned vLLM — are you relying on any custom kernels or modified attention layers? Or standard HF transformers and TGI-compatible endpoints?
[01:27] Miguel: Mostly standard. We do a couple of custom ops for sparse attention in the long context stuff, but for the majority it's TGI compatible. The vLLM cluster runs LoRA fine tuned models and we have a small ensemble stack.
[01:40] Liam (Solutions Eng): Okay, that's helpful. Redwood's compatibility matrix covers TGI/vLLM-style runtimes; our onboarding flow includes a model import and a parity eval against your prompt set. We can usually run the same weights and quantization profiles to see latency and output differences.
[01:55] Owen (Security): A couple security questions: do you support customer-managed keys (we use AWS KMS), and how do audit logs look for inference requests? Also SSO — we use Okta.
[02:06] Jordan: Yes, for Private we support KMS integration and HSM in certain enterprise plans, and our Console exposes audit logs with token-level tracing. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. We'll attach our security pack.
[02:20] Miguel: Cool. On the eval parity side, how do you surface small differences — e.g., when we move from OpenAI to an open model on Redwood, prompt outputs change; do you run automatic reranking or guardrails?
[02:32] Samira: There are two pieces — first, we run a scoring/eval harness you provide (your prompt set + reference outputs) and report metrics like exact-match, BLEU-ish, and semantic similarity. Second, our Optimize tools recommend quantization profiles and batching configs to match throughput and cost. For production we also suggest a canary traffic policy so you can compare outputs live.
[02:51] Priya: What's the typical latency delta we should expect if we go from OpenAI to a Redwood-hosted open model?
[02:58] Liam: It depends on model size and quantization. For mid-sized models we typically see comparable p99s within 10–30% depending on batching; for very large models p99 may be higher unless you move to Dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs. Our Console shows token-level breakdowns so you can see where time is spent.
[03:16] Priya: Understood. On costs: we want predictable unit economics. If we start on Hosted and later purchase Dedicated, how seamless is the migration?
[03:24] Jordan: Pretty seamless — same API and model versions are supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We keep the same route and can pin model versions. Migration mostly involves capacity planning and adjusting autoscaling policies; we help with load testing.
[03:36] Miguel: For our batch vLLM jobs, we currently have custom KV cache management — would Redwood's runtime support prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputation?
[03:45] Samira: Yes, our serving runtime has KV cache management features and automatic prefix caching for repeated contexts. We can usually map your caching pattern to our runtime; for custom sparse attention ops we'd want to test in the pilot.
[03:57] Owen: Any compliance certs we should know? SOC 2? EU data residency?
[04:02] Jordan: SOC 2 Type II is available for enterprise customers; we have EU regions and private deployment options for data residency. We'll include the certs in the security pack.
[04:12] Miguel: About model weights — will we be able to bring our fine-tuned LoRA weights and run them on Dedicated?
[04:18] Samira: Yes, you can bring weights. We'll handle conversion if necessary and recommend quantization. We also preserve KV cache and tokenizer settings to keep parity.
[04:27] Priya: For the pilot, what would you need from us to get started?
[04:30] Samira: Best is a canonical prompt set (we can handle anonymization), sample inputs, an indication of traffic distribution over 48–72h, and a target SLO (p95/p99). We'll create a benchmark harness and run against both Redwood Hosted and your vLLM baseline.
[04:45] Miguel: We can share that. Also want to simulate burst traffic patterns — is your Dedicated autoscaling able to handle sudden spikes?
[04:52] Liam: Yes, Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity options; we can set thresholds based on latency SLOs and have fallback policies to a cheaper model variant if capacity is constrained.
[05:05] Priya: How do you manage fallbacks without changing behavior too much? We worry about quality regressions if routing flips between model variants.
[05:12] Samira: We do gradual canary rollouts with A/B comparisons and automatic rollback if quality metrics drop. You can also pin routes to exact model versions for critical paths.
[05:24] Miguel: Any gotchas around tokenizer differences when switching providers? We've had tokenization cause length mismatches before.
[05:29] Liam: Good point — tokenizer parity is part of the import process. We'll surface token counts and mapping differences and recommend truncation/prefix strategies.
[05:39] Owen: Network topology question — for Private on prem, does Redwood require an outbound control plane? Can everything be air-gapped?
[05:46] Jordan: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option; fully air-gapped on-prem is supported for high compliance customers but usually involves additional packaging and legal steps. We'll outline the options in the security doc.
[05:59] Priya: Pricing — ballpark numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:03] Jordan: We'll send tailored pricing after we see your workloads, but Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Dedicated involves reserved capacity contracts with monthly commits; the unit token cost typically drops with Dedicated. We'll include a cost model in the follow-up.
[06:18] Miguel: For the benchmark, can you mimic our exact vLLM stack config — including LoRA adapters?
[06:23] Samira: We can load LoRA adapters and run the same seed/value for deterministic eval where possible. We'll note any nondeterminism in sampling too.
[06:34] Priya: Great. Any integration with our observability stack? We use Datadog and internal tracing.
[06:39] Liam: Yes, Redwood Console integrates with tracing hooks and can export metrics to Datadog; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[06:47] Miguel: Would love to see an example of the Console token-level breakdown and rollback policy in action.
[06:52] Jordan: We'll schedule a short demo of the Console with your team — Samira can run through the rollback and canary features.
[07:00] Samira: Quick note — latency numbers can shift with quantization. If you want to preserve accuracy we can recommend 8-bit quant profiles that balance cost and p99.
[07:10] Owen: For KMS, we need to ensure envelope encryption and key rotation policies — are those supported?
[07:15] Jordan: Yes, envelope encryption and rotation are supported for enterprise/private. We'll include the KMS integration details in the pack.
[07:25] Priya: Sounds good. Let's recap the action items and next steps.
[07:29] Jordan: Recap: Jordan will send security pack and SOC2 certs; Samira will draft pilot + benchmark script; Miguel will provide prompt set and traffic profile; schedule SE networking deep dive week of 11/16. Any objections?
[07:42] Priya: No objections, that's fine. One ask — can the pilot include a short production-like canary with real traffic? We can route 2% traffic if we have confidence in the metrics.
[07:53] Samira: Yes, we can do a 1–5% canary and capture metrics side-by-side. We'll define rollback thresholds.
[08:01] Miguel: I'll get the prompt set by Friday.
[08:04] Owen: I'll gather our KMS and encryption requirements doc and share.
[08:08] Jordan: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and calendar invites.
[08:13] Priya: Thanks all.
[08:16] [call ends]

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings — e.g., vLLM sometimes transcribed as "v l m"; speaker labels may shift in a few segments. The team agreed on a pilot focusing on parity and a security review.
